_comment: TASK-116 P6 -- the capability table: what a human must be able to do in each game,
and which declared InputMap action is supposed to deliver it.
Why this exists: P1..P5 can all be green on a game nobody can actually play. A Lunar
Lander whose only key is 'thrust' passes P1 (it draws), P2 (the key responds), P3 (the
loop runs) and, if the README documents the one key, P5 as well -- and it is still not
a game. P6 is the missing half: every row names a capability and the observable that
must move when that capability's action is injected, and the gate checks each row
against the same attributable evidence P2 collects.
The table is authored by hand -- that part is judgement and is meant to be argued with.
Every row of it is then machine-checked -- that part is evidence.
'observable' is a substring of a changed state key, and may list alternatives with '|':
a turn-based game legitimately refuses a move (a wall, the board edge, an illegal
direction) and records the refusal in its own exported counter, so 'the key did
something' is true either way.
Where a game had NO exported refusal counter, TASK-116 added one (`frogger.RejectedSteps`,
`pacman.RejectedSteps`, `flappy.Restarts`). That is not a way to make the gate green: it is
the project's own design convention #1 ('observable state must be a Godot property') applied
to a case it had missed -- without it, 'the frog cannot hop down from the start row' and
'the down key is not wired at all' produced byte-identical evidence.
'missing' records a capability that no declared action delivers yet -- the gate reports
it as a FAIL and the defect register carries it with a proposed patch. Rows are removed
from 'missing' only when the action really exists and really responds.
_agent_thresholds_comment: TASK-124 C -- the model-in-the-loop playability thresholds for --agent=jev.
A NeoHorse-Jev answer is typed, not free text: `noul` returns a P(true) and `score`
returns an expected level on an ORDERED criteria list. Those two numbers are the
model's opinion, so they only become a gate verdict through a threshold -- and a
threshold is a choice, so it is configurable here rather than hard-coded in the agent.
*** STILL UNCALIBRATED. The values below are FITTED FOR SEPARATION, not calibrated
probabilities *** (TASK-128). The vendor reports no NLL/Brier/ECE for NeoHorse-Jev and
warns: 'Set thresholds on an independent dataset.' We now do set them on our own
labelled data -- positives: runs/playability/agent-jev/<game>/agent.json (the 20 fixed
games, all P1..P6 green); negatives: runs/playability/agent-jev-neg/<game>/agent.json
(the pre-fix exports that really are input-dead). 20 positives / 16 negatives, one
independent observation per game (the gate hands the agent the same state for all of
its calls, so repeated answers are not extra samples). Fit: tools/agent_threshold_calibrate.py
-- sweep both thresholds over the observed values and count misclassifications.
What the fit found (runs/playability/agent-thresholds-fit.json): NOTHING separates
cleanly. `noul.responses_to_input` is the only question with real signal (fixed-game
median 0.4555 vs broken-game median 0.1534) and it still overlaps; `playable_frame` and
`no_render_failure` overlap almost completely (the broken builds still draw a correct
frame -- the defect is that input does nothing); and `score`/brokenness carries NO
separation at all (best single-rule sweep = 13 errors of 36). So `score_max_expected`
is left at its prior 2.5: it is a loose upper guard, not a discriminator, and tightening
it would only add false alarms.
Chosen: noul_min_p_true 0.25 (prior 0.5) -- the joint minimum, 3 errors / 36 games vs
11 / 36 for the prior; it flags 1 fixed game (game2048, noul 0.0401) and passes 2 broken
ones (frogger 0.3835, puzzlebobble 0.3302). `uncalibrated` STAYS true: separation on ~36
samples is not a probability calibration and an ECE here would be a number about noise.
TASK-124's old plan ('flip uncalibrated to false with the measured ECE') is therefore
explicitly NOT carried out -- that is a finding, not an omission.
Calibration done in TASK-128: positives are runs/playability/agent-jev (the 20 fixed
games, all P1..P6 green); negatives are runs/playability/agent-jev-neg (16 of the 20
dist/exe-task109-pre-fix exports -- breakout, pong, snake and tetris measured playable
even pre-fix, so they are NOT negatives). Both thresholds were swept over the observed
values and the pair with the fewest misclassifications was written here. See
recovery/reports/TASK-128-REPORT.md section 4 and
runs/playability/agent-thresholds-fit.json.

_model_player_change_margin_comment: TASK-135 §1.B -- the MODEL-PLAYER change test's TWO margins, declared side by side.
The change test is the whole game-facing half of the TASK-132 model-player criterion:
a step counts as 'the game responded' only when the action window BEATS its own
equal-length NO-INPUT control window.  There are two independent terms (TASK-132 §1.1
step 5), and until TASK-135 only one of them had a margin:
* pixels    -- `px > max(2.5 * control, 40)`.  The 2.5x is TASK-132's own, higher than
the gate's `arm_evidence` 1.5x because the two windows here are MEASURED
windows of a live game (the gate's are bracketed by its own MCP round
trips), so the comparison carries more timing slack; 40 px is the gate's
'a genuine frame-to-frame change, not noise'.
* gameplay  -- the declared observables must move MORE in the action window, where
'more' was the bare `>` -- NO margin at all.
TASK-134 §7.4 measured what that costs: `pong x jev x V3`'s PASS was carried by 3 of its
8 steps being decided by the gameplay term ALONE (`ctl_px == px` on those steps), and one
of the three won by 766.2 vs 641.1 -- a factor of 1.19.  A game that is animating by
itself (pong's ball keeps flying) therefore cleared the term by a hair.  TASK-135 §1.B
asked for a declared, stricter margin and forbade using it to turn a verdict green.
`baseline` is the TASK-132 rule, unchanged, and since TASK-136 §1.A.1 it is the CONTROL
reading rather than the pass criterion: it is still computed and reported for every step
and every run, so nothing about the old reading was lost or rewritten.
`strict` asks the same question with a margin: the declared observables must move at
least 2x as far as they moved in the control window.
Why 2x:
* it is the example the task itself gives ('>= 2x the control window's noise/
displacement'),
* it is the margin the PIXEL term has always required (2.5x >= 2x), so after TASK-135
the two terms are held to the same order of magnitude instead of one having a margin
and the other none,
* and it is what separates the measured edge steps from the measured real ones on the
only run that has ever been decided by this term: `pong x jev x V3`'s steps 2 and 7
sat at 1.09x and 1.19x (edge, dropped), while step 3 sat at 2.35x (kept).
`gameplay_min_movement` is the floor for the zero-control case: with the control window
carrying no movement at all the ratio is undefined, and 1.0 is what 'the declared
quantity really moved' means (a board string that advanced, or one pixel of travel).
Neither number is a verdict by itself: EVERY step is scored under BOTH margins, both
verdicts are written into `player.json` (`verdict` + `strict_verdict` +
`baseline_verdict`), and the steps the two readings disagree about are listed as
`change_margin_edge_steps`.
TASK-136 §1.A.1 changed WHICH margin is the criterion, not the margins themselves:
`default_margin` is now `strict`, so `player.json -> verdict` is `PASS` only when the
strict margin passes.  A run the strict margin refuses while the baseline accepts is
written `PASS(baseline only)` and carries `counts_as_pass: false` -- it is reported, and
it is never counted as a pass.  `--change-margin` still selects either reading for a
specific run (both are always reported beside each other).

_model_player_window_comment: TASK-139 §1.A -- the DECLARED MINIMUM MEASUREMENT WINDOW, and the `WINDOW_TOO_SHORT` state.
Why this exists.  `--window-frames` is a NOMINAL budget: the loop waits until the game's
own `Engine.get_frames_drawn()` has advanced by that many frames, so the length a window
really achieves is a MEASURED quantity, and TASK-138 defect ⑧ already records it per step
(`frame_alignment.steps[].control_frames` / `.action_frames`).  Before this declaration the
tool had no way to say 'this judgement was made over a window too short to contain a game
reaction': a 3-frame window and a 300-frame window produced the same two verdict strings.
`min_frames` is deliberately NOT a PASS gate.  It can only take a run OUT of PASS: a run
whose control or action window came out shorter than this is written
`WINDOW_TOO_SHORT <verdict>` with `counts_as_pass: false`, and the measured spans stay in
the artifact.  It never turns a non-PASS into a PASS and it does not move either ruler's
formula (both are unchanged from TASK-135/TASK-136).
BASIS for 20 (measured, not guessed): TASK-138 recorded 61 steps across its 20 games, and
the achieved span of BOTH windows ran 29..34 drawn frames -- no window in that sweep was
ever shorter than 29.  20 is therefore BELOW every recorded run's own floor: it flags
nothing in that batch's evidence, it is comfortably above one MCP round trip (TASK-138
defect ⑧ measured a single round trip at 30..120 drawn frames, so a window is at most that
resolution), and at ~60 Hz it is about a third of a second -- 1/3 of the 1.0 s the change
test compares against.  A window shorter than 20 drawn frames cannot contain a full
input-release -> game-loop -> observable read-back cycle with any margin, which is exactly
the judgement this state refuses to make.
TASK-140 §1.A.1 adds a SECOND, higher number to the same block: `reporting_frames`.  The
two are not the same statement.  `min_frames` says 'below this, no judgement at all may be
made'.  `reporting_frames` says 'below this, a judgement may be made and reported, but it
may not be reported AS A PASS', because TASK-139 §A.4 measured that at w30 the same game
with the same command and the same code changed verdict class between rounds (4 of 5 probed
games), while w90 did not.  A run below `reporting_frames` keeps its measured verdict, its
per-step evidence and its frames; it carries `reporting_window.at_reporting_window: false`
and `counts_as_pass: false`, and `qualified_verdict` appends '[reference only: ...]'.

model_player_window.declared_by: TASK-139 §1.A: the minimum.  TASK-140 §1.A.1: the reporting window.
model_player_window.reporting_basis: MEASURED (TASK-139 §A.4: three complete w30 probes and two complete w90 probes of the same five games, same command, same code): at w30 the per-game verdict was NOT reproducible across rounds -- asteroids, tetris, pong and breakout each changed class between rounds (4 of 5), with the mechanism located per step (Engine.get_frames_drawn() span jitter plus an occasionally missing ack_result); at w90 the two complete rounds agreed per game on the same five games.  The reporting window is therefore 90: below it a verdict is still measured, still recorded and still printed, but it is a REFERENCE reading and can never count as a pass.

The SAME loader reads `reporting_frames` and `summarise` writes `player.json -> reporting_window` / `-> verdict_context` / `-> qualified_verdict`, forcing `counts_as_pass = false` for a run whose nominal `--window-frames` is below it.  `gate.json -> model_player_criterion` reads the same block and the run's `player.json -> verdict_context`.

_model_player_stability_comment: TASK-140 §1.A.2 -- `UNSTABLE`: the cross-round judgement, and the reason it exists.
TASK-139 §A.4 measured that the SAME game, at the SAME window, with the SAME command and
the SAME code, can read a different verdict in a second independent complete run (w30: 4 of
5 probed games changed class).  A verdict that is not reproducible is not evidence of a
class, so a single run may no longer be reported as a PASS on its own: >= 2 independent
complete runs at the same window are compared, and any disagreement makes the game
UNSTABLE.
The comparison is on the verdict CLASS, not on the string: `PASS` and `PASS(baseline only)`
are different classes (TASK-136), and the measurement states `WINDOW_TOO_SHORT ...` /
`MODEL_FIXED_POINT` / `MODEL_NO_PROGRESS` are classes of their own, so a flip between any
two of them is a disagreement and cannot be hidden.
`UNSTABLE` can only ever REMOVE a pass.  It never turns a non-PASS into a PASS, it does not
rewrite any run's own `player.json`, and the per-step divergence points it lists are the
place to look for the mechanism (`injected` / `accepted` / `ack_missing` / `changed` /
`changed_strict` / `step_verdict`), not a re-reading of the game.
Two things `UNSTABLE` is NOT:
* it is NOT a window-length judgement.  `SENSITIVE` (TASK-139) compares TWO WINDOWS of one
game; `UNSTABLE` compares TWO ROUNDS at one window.  They are reported side by side and
neither may be used to excuse the other.
* it is NOT a replacement for the per-step evidence.  A stable PASS at the reporting
window still carries its `steps.jsonl`, its frames and its anchors.

model_player_stability.rule: the same game at the same window, run for >= `min_rounds` INDEPENDENT complete rounds, is UNSTABLE when its verdict class is not identical in every round; an UNSTABLE game is listed with the divergent rounds and with the per-step divergence points (which step, which criterion), and it NEVER counts as a pass.  Fewer rounds than `min_rounds` is INSUFFICIENT_ROUNDS, which is not a judgement and is not a pass either.
model_player_stability.how_used: `tools/playtest_player.py` -> `stability_summary` / `stability_from_paths` / `verdict_class` / `divergence_between`, driven by `playtest_player.py stability --run <player.json> --run <player.json> [--out FILE]`; this batch's sweeps write `player.json -> verdict_context` with `window_frames` and `round` per run, which is what the comparison reads.
model_player_stability.basis: MEASURED: TASK-139 §A.4, three complete w30 probes of five games (4 of 5 flip) against two complete w90 probes (0 of 5 flip).
not_a_loosening: an UNSTABLE set can never pass: `counts_as_pass` is false unless EVERY round is a literal PASS
no verdict string is rewritten; the per-round `player.json` files keep their own readings
the class comparison is over the classes TASK-136/TASK-139 already defined, so a flip between `PASS` and `PASS(baseline only)` counts as a disagreement

model_player_refusal.rule: a step the game's own exported counters record as a deliberate refusal is (1) removed from the model-player FAIL set, (2) removed from the rate's denominator, and (3) NEVER counted as progress.  A run is FAIL when every rated step was refused and no step produced real progress (`refusal_only_run`), and INCONCLUSIVE when fewer than `min_real_progress_steps` steps of real progress remain after the carve-out.
model_player_refusal.evidence_source: the game's own exported state delta for the step (`steps.jsonl -> state_delta`), matched against `games.<game>.refusal_evidence.game_side_fields` / `.keys`; the model's own statement is never used
model_player_refusal.how_used: tools/playtest_player.py `step_refusal_record` (per step, written as `steps.jsonl -> step_refusal`), `_summarise_core` (the FAIL set, the rated denominator, `refusal_only_run`, `real_progress_step_count`); the numbers are in `player.json -> refusal_boundary`
model_player_refusal.basis: MEASURED: the PASS rule needs >= 8 injected steps and the accepted-and-changed bar is 0.75, so a run that met the bar with no refusals always has >= 6 real progress steps; 4 is below that and half the minimum step count.
not_a_loosening: the carve-out can only remove a FAIL the GAME ITSELF recorded as a refusal
it can never turn a 'not changed' into a 'changed': refusals are excluded from both the FAIL set and the progress set
`refusal_only_run` is an explicit FAIL branch, so 'all refused, zero progress' cannot PASS
a run with no refusals has an empty refused set and every number is the pre-TASK-139 number

gameplay_observables.rule: a changed state key counts as GAMEPLAY only when it (a) contains one of this game's `items` AND (b) does NOT match the uniform META patterns in tools/playability_gate.py: clocks (`Ticks`, `Elapsed`, `_logTimer`), input accounting (`Input*`, `LastEvent`, `LastDir`, `LastMoveDir`), refusals (`Rejected*`), digests (`*Hash`), UI labels (`*.text`), input intents (`DirectionX`/`DirectionY`, `Facing`, `AngleIndex`), mode flags (`Paused`, `GameOver`, `LoseReason`), seeds, `Moved`.  META wins over `items`, so a declaration cannot re-admit a meta key by listing it.  A position, a velocity, a board, a score or a consumed-object counter DOES count, because that is the world moving; an input acknowledgement is not.
gameplay_observables.how_used: tools/playability_gate.py `is_gameplay_key` / `gameplay_changes` / `arm_evidence`; P2 requires every declared action to move one of these (or pixels) past its own no-input control window, and P3 requires gameplay progress somewhere in the run

refusal_evidence.what: how this project records a DELIBERATE refusal of an input (a wall, the board edge, an illegal direction).  Used only as P2's carve-out: an action with no gameplay change is accepted when one of these moved AND at least one other action of the same game did move a gameplay observable -- so 'everything was refused because the game is dead' still fails.
refusal_evidence.rule: an arm is `refused` when one of `keys` is among its changed state keys (or a changed string value contains one of `value_words`), the same was NOT true of its own no-input control window, and the arm moved neither a gameplay observable nor pixels
refusal_evidence.provenance: TASK-116 wrote the convention down: where a game had no exported refusal counter one was added (`frogger.RejectedSteps`, `pacman.RejectedSteps`, `flappy.Restarts`)
refusal_evidence.how_used: tools/playability_gate.py `refusal_hit` / `arm_evidence`; recorded per action in gate.json -> criteria.P2.gameplay_evidence
refusal_evidence.identifies: `td_place` on a cell where a tower may not be built (occupied, or not enough gold): `InputRejectedPlaces` advances while `TowersPlaced` and `Gold` stay put.  Measured on TASK-138 scripted steps 6/9/12.  The attempt counter `InputPlaces` is deliberately NOT in this list.
refusal_evidence.how_read: the game's own exported property, read inside the game process by tools/playability_gate.probe_state_source() (executed through the MCP tool `running_game_execute_gdscript`), sampled before and after each injection and diffed into `steps.jsonl -> state_delta`; this tool then matches the diffed key against `game_side_fields`.  The model's own statement is never used.
refusal_evidence.step_rule: a step is a LEGAL REFUSAL when `game_side_fields` (or `keys`) appears among the keys of `steps.jsonl -> state_delta` for that step -- i.e. the game itself recorded that it saw the input and refused the move.  Such a step is removed from the FAIL set and from the rate's denominator, is NEVER counted as real progress, and the run must still show `min_real_progress_steps` steps of real progress (`model_player_refusal`) or it cannot PASS.  A run in which EVERY rated step was refused and nothing advanced is an explicit FAIL (`refusal_only_run`).
